The Commissioner will take into consideration the amount of any common component permitted in other color additives, food additives, and pesticide chemical residues, as well as the similar biological activity produced by that substance when establishing tolerances.

21 CFR 70.11(c) states that pesticide chemicals may also cause pharmacological or biological effects similar or related to such effects caused by color additives, and, in the absence of evidence to the contrary, those that do so will be considered to have additive toxic effects [3].

This exemption does not apply unless the conditions in §71.37(a) are met, including that no animals used in such investigations or their products (e.g., milk, eggs) shall be used for food purposes without prior authorization from the FDA based on public health data [1].

The person responsible for shipping or delivering the product must maintain adequate records that include the name and post-office address of the expert to whom the color additive is shipped, the date, quantity, and batch or code mark of each shipment or delivery, and these records must be kept for a period of 2 years after such shipment and delivery [2]. These records must be available for inspection and copying upon request by a properly authorized employee of the FDA at reasonable times [2].
